region.text: England and Wales, declared a Commonwealth by the Rump Parliament on 19 May 1649

events.note: England and Wales are ruled by the Commonwealth, which the Rump Parliament declared on 19 May 1649. Page: 'An Act declaring England to be a Commonwealth', adopted by the Rump Parliament on 19 May 1649, declared the people of England 'and of all the Dominions and Territories thereunto belonging' a Commonwealth. Seam repair: the 1 January 1650 anchor still draws England and Wales (649 cells) as kingdom-of-england (the 1649 found and merge events moved only 28 cells to the Commonwealth), and the land passed only at the 1653 keyframe snap (644 cells), so 1650-1652 were drawn as a kingdom that ended on 19 May 1649. Dated 1 January 1650 as the earliest moment inside this window; the true date is May 1649 (previous window). Reviewer: keyframe_overrides/0 is its companion, so the 1653 snap does not drop five coastal England and Wales cells to nobody.

region.text: Jiangnan Province, the old Ming South Zhili ('Now Jiangsu & Shanghai', 'Now Anhui')

events.note: Anhui is Qing land: Jiangnan Province, the old Ming South Zhili (now Anhui, Jiangsu and Shanghai), was 'established in 1645 during the Qing conquest of Ming'. Jiangnan page: it 'administered the area of the earlier Ming province of Nanzhili'; its table reads 'Now Jiangsu & Shanghai' and 'Now Anhui'. Southern Ming page: Nanjing surrendered on 8 June 1645, and the page names no Anhui, Jiangsu or Henan land as Southern Ming after that. Seam repair: the anchor of 1 January 1650 holds 465 Anhui cells and 10 cells of the Shanghai coast (121.0-121.7 E) as Southern Ming until the 1653 keyframe snap hands them to the Qing. Dated 1 January 1650 as the earliest moment inside this window; the true date is 1645. Reviewer: region widened from Anhui to the whole of Jiangnan so that the 10 Southern Ming cells on the Shanghai coast pass too (the gain takes only the counterpart's cells; events/2 takes nobody's).

region.text: Jiangsu and Shanghai, the eastern half of Jiangnan Province (the old Ming South Zhili)

events.note: Jiangsu and Shanghai are Qing land, the eastern half of Jiangnan Province, 'established in 1645 during the Qing conquest of Ming'. Seam repair, companion of events/1: 212 Jiangsu and 20 Shanghai cells are nobody's on 1 January 1650 and stay so until the 1653 keyframe snap gives them to the Qing. Jiangnan page: it 'administered the area of the earlier Ming province of Nanzhili' (its table reads 'Now Jiangsu & Shanghai'). Southern Ming page: Nanjing taken by the Qing in June 1645; no Jiangsu land named as Southern Ming after that. Dated 1 January 1650 as the earliest moment inside this window; the true date is 1645.

region.text: the Shan states (without Kengtung) and the Kachin hills, the land the Toungoo ledger gives the state in 1653 (ledger /78)

events.note: The Shan states and the Kachin hills are Toungoo land: the restored kingdom encompassed 'Lower Burma, Upper Burma, Shan States and Lan Na by 1622'. Seam repair: the 1648 Southern Ming shape (Cliopatria's Ming frontier) holds 186 Kachin and 90 Shan cells in Burma until the 1653 keyframe snap, after which they are nobody's until Toungoo's 1659 keyframe, so 1653-1658 show a grey hole. The Southern Ming page has the Yongli emperor flee into Burma only in late January 1659 and names no Southern Ming land in Burma before. The Restored Toungoo page says nothing on the Kachin hills; the dossier's ledger /78 has them (and not Kengtung) from 1653.

region.text: Kebbi: Leka, Surame and Birnin Kebbi in the Rima and Zamfara valleys, the heartland of the kingdom

events.note: Kebbi keeps its heartland round Birnin Kebbi: it 'ceased to be a great power' by the mid 17th century but 'remained one of the leading states in Hausaland at the turn of the 19th century'. Repair: ledger /4 (1650, end of the Hausa tributes, region Hausaland) releases all 706 cells, heartland included, so the kingdom has 0 cells from 1650 to 1808. Kebbi page: in 1556 'the Hausa states stopped paying tribute'; in 1808 Abdullahi dan Fodio 'defeated the forces of Kebbi'. The heartland is the dossier's own keyframe region; the gain takes only nobody's land (103 cells; Dendi keeps its 53).

correction.text: 1653: England, Wales, Scotland and Ireland form the Commonwealth of England, Scotland and Ireland. Cliopatria's 1653 shape with every England and Wales cell.

keyframe_overrides.why: Reviewer's companion of events/0: once events/0 gives the Commonwealth all of England and Wales in 1650, the 1653 snap to Cliopatria's shape drops five coastal cells it lacks (Tyneside, the Northumberland, Lincolnshire and Kent coasts, Lleyn) to nobody until 1660; the Commonwealth page has the act of 19 May 1649 cover England 'and all the Dominions and Territories thereunto belonging' and the state enlarged in 1653 as the Commonwealth of England, Scotland and Ireland. The shape gains exactly those five cells (1327 to 1332).

region.text: Sweden inside its present border: the stray Danish-Norwegian cells in Dalarna, Västerbotten, Kronoberg and Västra Götaland

rulings.why: Against the current dossiers the ruling acts in 1658 only, on 19 cells Sweden's 1658 keyframe claims that the size rule gave to Denmark-Norway: Kronoberg 8, Kalmar 3 and Värmland 4 (Swedish land) and Västra Götaland 4 (Dalsland and northern Bohuslän). The Roskilde page (26 February O.S. / 8 March 1658) has the 'immediate cession' of Scania, Blekinge, Halland and the Norwegian province of Bohuslän; no page lists Danish land in Sweden proper in these years.
